did_you_know.text: The prophet describes a determination not to remain silent or rest for Zion and Jerusalem’s sake until her righteousness and salvation shine before everyone like a light and a burning torch.
According to the verse, the nations and kings will see Jerusalem’s righteousness and glory, and she will receive a new name chosen by the Lord.
Jerusalem is described as a “crown of splendor” and as a royal symbol held in the hand of the Lord and in the hand of her God.

Jerusalem will no longer be called “Forsaken,” nor will her land be called “Desolate.” Instead, she will be called “My Delight Is in Her,” and her land “Married”—names expressing affection and a renewed relationship.

The relationship between Jerusalem and her people is compared to marriage: as a young man marries a virgin, so her people will be joined to her; and the Lord will rejoice over her as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride.
The Lord appoints watchmen on Jerusalem’s walls whose duty is to remain constantly alert, day and night, and to remind the Lord.
The watchmen are commanded not to give the Lord silence until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her a praise in the earth. In this way, prayer is presented as part of the expectation of redemption.
The Lord swears by his right hand and his mighty arm that Jerusalem’s harvest will no longer be given to her enemies. Instead, those who gather it will eat and drink it in the holy courts.
As the people return, the gates are to be cleared, the road prepared and cleaned of stones, and a banner raised for the nations to mark and announce the way.
The message is to reach the ends of the earth: “See, your salvation is coming.” The verse presents salvation as accompanied by reward and recompense from the Lord.
